title: Halting of the pair extraction machine
statement: Let $first$ and $second$ be Boolean flags, and let $x$ and $rest$ be Boolean words. For every pair of Boolean words $pre$ and $a$ satisfying $x=pre\mathbin{++}rest$, the pair extraction machine started with input head just after $pre$, work tape containing $a$ with its head at position $|a|$, and empty output reaches a halting configuration after some number $t$ of steps with $t\le 3|rest|+2|a|+5$. Its output is $(a\mathbin{++}b$ if $first$ is true, and the empty word otherwise$)\mathbin{++}(c$ if $second$ is true, and the empty word otherwise$)$ when pair decoding of $rest$ yields $(b,c)$, and is empty when that decoding is undefined.
hypotheses_covered: For every Boolean word pre and Boolean word a
